change_scope: B4-only physical placement policy and isolated artifacts; B2/B3 remain immutable

global_route.reason: Return to B2's stable single-RRR policy; B4's independent variable is placement.

candidates.rtl_or_constraint_change: B4-only placement policy: read the immutable B2 placed ODB, run one RUDY-based routability-driven global respread from existing coordinates, then legalize into a new B4 checkpoint. RTL/netlist/fence geometry are unchanged.
candidates.expected_central_corridor_effect: RUDY inflation acts on the measured local demand peaks before legalization, spreading entry points and pin demand without changing logical cones.

risk.function: none expected; mapped netlist is byte-compared against B2
risk.timing: moderate; HPWL can increase and must be reported after routing/CTS
risk.area: none at netlist level; placement footprint and four fences are unchanged
risk.physical: moderate; global respread can fail convergence or legalization

candidates.mapped_assertion_and_workload_effect: No functional change; nevertheless rerun cheap 9/9, mapped 20/20, workload 6/6, and comparator/locality assertions before placement.
candidates.rollback: Discard only the isolated B4 directory; B2/B3 and their ODBs remain byte-identical.
cheap_gates: central writeback comparator internal sink pins == 0
candidates.expected_improvement_basis: B2 already reduced the problem to 39 low-magnitude overflow edges, 31 in the central corridor. B3 proved that extra RRR without placement change thrashes (46 to 5641). Routability-driven placement is the smallest standard physical intervention that directly changes demand at all measured hotspots before the one allowed route.

candidates.rejection: B3 empirical evidence shows ten RRR iterations increased residual 46 to 5641.
The comparator cone did not recur and mapped/workload contracts pass; a functional redesign is broader and riskier than a placement-only routability ECO.
